online_combined.overlap_note: Segmentation is by Shopify sourceName, which is mutually exclusive by construction, so no duplicate order IDs exist across segments in this pull. Prior run's overlap figure (2) reflected a manual customer-level reconciliation that was not repeated this run.

funnel_7d.step_completion_rate_caveat: Mobile view_to_atc dropped from 3.39% (19-25 Jul) to 2.40% this window while desktop's atc_to_checkout jumped from 36.84% to 96.13% -- driven by desktop begin_checkout events (149) now exceeding desktop add_to_cart events (155) almost 1:1. Real event counts (unaffected by the GA4 F12 tracking break), but worth a manual check for a checkout-entry path that bypasses add_to_cart tracking on desktop.

ga4_capture_rate.capture_pct_caveat: Small-sample week (10 orders); a single mis-tagged order would move this +/-10pp. 30-day context below is more stable.

cart_cliff_7d.desktop_anomaly_note: Desktop began_checkout (149, real event count) exceeds desktop cart_page_users (96) this window, so progression_pct >100% -- some desktop begin_checkout events are firing without a tracked /checkout/cart pageview (e.g. a quick-buy path). Real data, not a calculation error; treat gap_multiple as directional only until this path is confirmed.
cart_cliff_7d.interpretation: Low bounce + high scroll + high rage clicks = users are stuck, not leaving. Mobile-specific overlay failure, now compounded: mobile cart rage clicks nearly doubled (538 -> 1059) after the 3 Aug deployment added a coupon/offer module on top of the existing login wall (see F1, F14).

sessions_7d.caveat: Window includes 1 Aug, the day GA4's engaged-session/bounce tracking broke sitewide (finding F12). A live spot-check today (4 Aug) found GA4 has since retroactively reprocessed 1 Aug back to normal ranges (e.g. mobile bounce 41.6% fresh vs the 99.7% recorded live that day) -- the bounce/engagement figures above use the corrected fresh pull, not the stale pre-correction values still sitting in daily_device.csv. avg_session_duration_s is userEngagementDuration/sessions from daily_device.csv (a proxy; GA4's native averageSessionDuration metric was not re-pulled per-day to stay within budget).

metric_definitions.avg_engagement_s: GA4 userEngagementDuration / totalUsers, from a single fresh pull over the full window (already reflects GA4's post-correction reprocessing -- see sessions_7d.caveat)
metric_definitions.bounce_pct: GA4 bounceRate (session-scoped; unreliable on mid-funnel pages)

traffic_quality_7d.root_cause_finding: Bounce differences between landing pages are still driven mostly by channel, not page template. This window's Paid Social volume on /collections/rings still bounces high (87.5%) at low volume. But the two collections that carried the bulk of Paid Social traffic last snapshot -- /collections/all-rings (1,032 sessions) and /collections/all-earrings (787+773 sessions) -- have collapsed to near-zero Paid Social sessions this window (1 and 0 respectively), suggesting that spend/campaign activity paused or was redirected, not a page-level fix.
traffic_quality_7d.paid_social_volume_shift_note: /collections/all-rings and /collections/all-earrings had almost no Paid Social sessions this window (1 and 0 rows above 1 session), versus 1,032 and 787+773 in the 19-25 Jul snapshot. Worth confirming with the team whether campaigns targeting these collections were paused.

fold_analysis.caveat: One PDP measured directly. Doc height dropped from 15,804px (27 Jul) to 13,220px this run -- template got shorter -- but avg_scroll_depth_pct is unchanged at 18.26% (real Clarity figure for this window), so Reviews moved to a WORSE relative position (48.1% depth vs 41.4% previously) despite the shorter page. Scroll depth still clusters 15-23% across top PDPs sitewide (see pages_7d), suggesting the template generalises.

shopify_native_sessions.detail: Shopify native session analytics reports ~670 sessions/30d vs 425,524 in GA4. Expected — the storefront is headless. Ignore this metric.

ga4_engagement_break.detail: See finding F12: GA4 engaged-session/bounce tracking collapsed sitewide on 1 Aug and recurred on 3 Aug (day after a deployment). New this run: a live pull today (4 Aug) found GA4 had already retroactively reprocessed 1 Aug's bounce/engagement figures back to normal ranges (e.g. mobile bounce 41.6% fresh vs 99.7% recorded live) -- the GA4 property self-corrects after some delay, but daily_device.csv and daily_pagetype.csv (pulled during the live defect window) still hold the stale pre-correction numbers and should be refreshed on the next data-catchup run. Unresolved whether the underlying GTM->GA4 tag-firing defect will recur on a future day; the console warning was still reproducing as of the 4 Aug morning check referenced in F12.

User-based, not event counts. biggest_leak.detail: Homepage->Collection loss eased slightly from 66.04% (19-25 Jul) to 56.97% this window, though it remains the single biggest drop in the journey. Mobile (57.26% lost) is still worse than desktop (55.30% lost), though the gap between them has narrowed.

heatmap_7d.note: Clarity's API does not expose heatmap images. It does expose the underlying data those images visualise: click distribution by element and scroll depth per page. That is what is recorded here.

by_funnel_stage.observation: Popup pressure eased slightly vs 19-25 Jul (10.3x nav) but is still ~9x the top genuine nav link. Note the top two rows ('Yellow', 'MQ_AI', 'White') are product-variant clicks bleeding onto the homepage template, not homepage content itself -- likely from a merchandising carousel.

Consistent with 19-25 Jul: Add to Cart does not appear in the top 10 clicked elements despite 2,544 users. Variant selection ('Yellow', 'MH', 'MQ', 'CI') still dominates real interaction over add-to-cart -- visitors are configuring, not committing.

Materially different from the 19-25 Jul snapshot, as expected: the 3 Aug deployment added a new coupon/offer module (see F14) and this run pulled real per-page clicked-element data for cart (the prior snapshot only had rage-click data here). 'Proceed To Checkout' and 'Cart1/3' are new top elements from that module; the login-modal cluster ('REQUEST OTP', 'WELCOME TO LUCIRA', '100% Secured & Spam Free') is still present underneath it, confirming F1 (login wall) and F14 (possible second gate) are compounding, not replacing each other.

heatmap_7d.headline: Popup pressure eased somewhat sitewide (homepage popup:nav ratio 10.3 -> 9.15) but the cart page now carries a second layer of friction: the 3 Aug coupon/offer module ('Proceed To Checkout', 'Cart1/3') sits directly on top of the pre-existing login wall, and cart rage clicks nearly doubled (538 -> 1,059) in the same window. Homepage -> Collection is still the single biggest leak in the journey (56.97% lost) even though it improved from 66.04%.

findings.title: GA4 engaged-sessions/bounce tracking break recurred on 3 Aug -- the day after a deployment -- and is still live this morning
findings.evidence: First seen 1 Aug (engagementRate ~0-2.4%, bounceRate ~97-100% sitewide, all 6 reference pages x both devices). 2 Aug was completely normal (mobile bounce 43.4%, engaged 56.6%). Then 3 Aug -- the day immediately after a deployment the client flagged -- broke again, identically: mobile bounce 99.6%/engaged 0.4%, desktop bounce 99.1%; every checkout-journey page (cart, shipping, payment) plus both PLPs and both PDPs collapsed to 0-7% engaged on both devices. Funnel event counts (view_item 14,294 mobile/1,245 desktop, add_to_cart 384+54, begin_checkout 62+39, purchase=2, signup=57+3+1) and Clarity (11,505 mobile sessions, 544 rage clicks, 26.5% scroll -- all normal range) confirm real behaviour did not change either day; only GA4's engaged-session flag did. Live console check this morning (4 Aug, cart + homepage, 3 reloads): 'Skipped GTM->GA4: Missing data for: pageView' fired on 3/3 loads (up from 1/3 on 3 Aug) -- the defect has not self-resolved and is live right now. Timing (normal 2 Aug -> broken the day after the reported deployment -> still broken today) points to the deployment as the likely trigger; recommend checking the GTM container publish history against the deployment timestamp. Opened as T22, still open.

findings.title: Microsoft Clarity now also warns it isn't collecting some sessions, on every page load checked
findings.evidence: Live console check, 4 Aug (cart + homepage, 3 reloads): 'Data from this session is not being collected by Microsoft Clarity due to your configured project settings' fired on every load, more consistently than previously observed. Caveat: Clarity's own daily aggregate session counts (11,505-15,169 mobile sessions/day, 2-3 Aug) stayed in the normal range, so this may be specific to the automated test session's bot-like fingerprint rather than proof real sessions are being dropped. Recommend the client's team check Clarity project settings (recording quota, sampling rate, path/domain restrictions) to rule out any narrowing since the deployment.

findings.title: New cart coupon-apply flow may stack a second login gate on top of the existing OTP wall
findings.evidence: Clarity clicked-element data for /checkout/cart, 3 Aug, logs 209 clicks on text truncated as 'ApplyLogin to Unlock Coup...' -- ambiguous due to Clarity's ~25-character truncation, but reads as though applying a coupon may itself require login. If so this compounds F1 rather than relieving it. Needs a 2-minute manual click-through on the 'Apply Coupon' row to confirm scope.

findings.title: Discount-code hygiene: a staff to-do note was left as a live, customer-facing discount code
findings.evidence: Order #2480 (Rs 20,000, salesperson-assisted, 2 Aug) carries discount code text '500Lucira point + 166 additional discount - Need to add' for a Rs 666 discount -- an internal note, not a real code, visible on the order record. Order #2486 similarly shows a generic 'Custom discount' label rather than a named code. Both are manual/draft-order entries; named codes elsewhere (GRAND250 on #2493, GRAND750 on #2478) applied cleanly with no issues. Process fix, not a system bug.

findings.title: Cart heatmap succeeded for the first time -- reveals empty-cart sessions absorb real click volume
findings.evidence: Every prior cro_heatmap attempt on /checkout/cart failed outright (no matchable click text on an empty cart). Re-tested 4 Aug: two real elements do exist on the empty state and matched -- 'Cart1/3' step chrome (1,136 weight, the single hottest spot on the page) and 'Your cart is empty' messaging (272 weight). Suggests a real share of cart-page Clarity sessions are landing on an empty cart (direct visit, bookmark, post-removal return) rather than mid-checkout with an item -- a distinct population from the login-wall/coupon-module sessions the rest of F1/F14 describe.

findings.title: Two Playwright tools disagree on the reference PDP's page height by ~2x -- a measurement-methodology gap, not a site defect
findings.evidence: cro_fold_analysis reproduced 13,220px / 16.3 screens twice on 4 Aug (stable). cro_heatmap's full-page screenshot on the identical URL+device same day came back 26,440px -- nearly double -- because its slower full-page scroll triggers additional lazy-loaded sections (Story Behind the Product, store locator, reviews carousel, Our Process, lab-grown comparison table, Explore Our Range) that a single settle-wait doesn't load. Both numbers are 'correct' for what they measure; flagged so the two aren't quoted interchangeably.
